issue: Is a supervised release condition barring association with any person known or reasonably expected to be a member of or associated with a gang impermissibly vague or overbroad?
provision: 18 U.S.C. § 3583(d); U.S. Const. amend. V (due process vagueness)

sides.position: The gang-association condition is impermissibly vague or overbroad and should be vacated.
cases: United States v. Johnson, 626 F.3d 1085 (9th Cir. 2010)

sides.position: The gang-association condition, including a bar on associating with gang 'associates' or 'prospects,' is upheld.
cases: United States v. Marshall, 808 F. App'x 11 (2d Cir. 2020)
United States v. Romig, 933 F.3d 1004 (8th Cir. 2019)

sides.position: Because the circuits are split, any error is not plain, so the condition stands at this stage without a merits ruling.
cases: United States v. Blake, No. 24-2125 (6th Cir. 2026)

quote: Our sister circuits are split on whether such a prohibition on associating with gang “associates” is impermissibly vague or overbroad.
cite: United States v. Cortez Blake, No. 24-2125 (6th Cir. 2026)
